title: The transport of cohomology along the geometric Frobenius is an isomorphism
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme, put
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\Spec k$, let $a_Y:Y\to s$ be the structure
morphism, let $g_Y:Y\to Y$ be the geometric Frobenius
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed] and $g_s=\Spec(\operatorname{Frob}_q):s\to s$.
Let $\iota_N$ (for $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$), $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M)$,
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M)$, $\tau_M$ and $\tau_{c,M}$ (for $M\in
D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$) be the point transport, the exchange maps along the
Frobenius square, and the transports of ordinary and compactly supported
cohomology along $g_Y$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Then:

1. for every $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$, $\iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to
\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)$ is an isomorphism;

2. for every $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$,
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M\to Ra_{Y*}Lg_Y^*M$ and
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M):Lg_s^*Ra_{Y!}M\to Ra_{Y!}Lg_Y^*M$ are
isomorphisms in $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$;

3. consequently, for every $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$,
$\tau_M:\RGamma(Y,M)\to\RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ and
$\tau_{c,M}:\RGammac(Y,M)\to\RGammac(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ are isomorphisms, natural
in $M$, and so are the induced maps $\mathrm H^i(\tau_M)$ and
$\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M})$ on cohomology groups
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] for every integer $i$.

source.place: the symbols \sim on the first arrows of both displayed composites of node def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius (order 2061), asserted there without proof; also node lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description (order 2298), which calls the compact-support arrow 'the compact-support base-change isomorphism along the automorphism'; cf. Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II (literature/deligne-weil-II_PMIHES-1980-52.pdf), (1.1.7), p. 151, action by transport of structure

proof.text:
*Point transport, first map ($\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$).* By
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] (1), in the case $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, $g_s=\Spec(\gamma)$ is an
automorphism of $s$ with inverse $\Spec(\gamma^{-1})$. Hence $(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$ is an object of
$s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (an isomorphism is weakly etale), and the morphism
$g_s:(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)\to(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ used in
[def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] has the inverse
$g_s^{-1}:(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)\to(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$ (a morphism over $s$ because
$g_s\circ g_s^{-1}=\operatorname{id}$). A presheaf is a functor, so the restriction
$\operatorname{res}_{g_s}:N^i(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)\to N^i(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$ along an
isomorphism is bijective, with inverse the restriction along $g_s^{-1}$, for every term $N^i$ of $N$;
so $\operatorname{res}_{g_s}$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text:
*Point transport, second map.* Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (a term $N^i$).
By [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] $(g_s^{-1}\mathcal F)$ is the sheafification of the presheaf
$P(U\xrightarrow{u}s)=\varinjlim_{(V,\,U\to s\times_{s,g_s}V)}\mathcal F(V)$. An $s$-morphism
$U\to s\times_{s,g_s}V$, for $V=(V\xrightarrow{v}s)$, is the same as a morphism $t:U\to V$ with
$v\circ t=g_s\circ u$, and a morphism of indices $(V,t)\to(V',t')$ is an $s$-morphism $h:V\to V'$
with $h\circ t=t'$. The index $(V_U,t_U)=((U\xrightarrow{g_s\circ u}s),\operatorname{id}_U)$ is initial:
for any $(V,t)$ the only $h$ with $h\circ\operatorname{id}_U=t$ is $h=t$, and $t$ is an $s$-morphism
$(U,g_s u)\to(V,v)$ because $v t=g_s u$. Since $\mathcal F$ is contravariant, the colimit is attained at
this index: the insertion $\mathcal F(U\xrightarrow{g_su}s)\to P(U\xrightarrow{u}s)$ is bijective, and
these bijections are natural in $U$, so $P\cong\mathcal F\circ\Phi_{g_s}$ with
$\Phi_{g_s}(U\xrightarrow{u}s)=(U\xrightarrow{g_su}s)$. By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]
(1), $\Phi_{g_s}$ is an equivalence of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with itself, and it and its quasi-inverse
send coverings to coverings; an equivalence preserves fibre products, so $\mathcal F\circ\Phi_{g_s}$
satisfies the sheaf condition for every covering, i.e. $P$ is already a sheaf and the sheafification map
$P\to g_s^{-1}\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism. For $U=(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ the initial
index is $V=(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$ with $t=\operatorname{id}_s$, i.e. the $s$-morphism
$(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s):s\to s\times_{s,g_s}V$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]; so
$\operatorname{ins}:N^i(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)\to(g_s^{-1}N^i)(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ is an
isomorphism for every $i$, and $\operatorname{ins}$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text:
*Point transport, third map.* By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (3), for
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ the structure map $c^{g_s}_{A_{E,n}}:g_s^{-1}(A_{E,n})_s\to(A_{E,n})_s$ of
[def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$,
with $\Lambda_s=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_s$
[def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the structure map used in
[def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] is the composite of the canonical map
$g_s^{-1}\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_s\to\varprojlim_mg_s^{-1}(A_{E,m})_s$, an isomorphism by
[lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (2), and $\varprojlim_mc^{g_s}_{A_{E,m}}$, a limit of
isomorphisms by (3), hence an isomorphism. So $c^{g_s}_\Lambda:g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$ is an
isomorphism of sheaves of rings, in particular of $g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s$-modules. The derived tensor product
$g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}(-)$ is a functor of the second variable, so
$\operatorname{id}\otimes^Lc^{g_s}_\Lambda:g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s\to
g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}\Lambda_s=Lg_s^*N$ is an isomorphism, and so is its composite with
the unit isomorphism $g_s^{-1}N\cong g_s^{-1}N\otimes^L_{g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s}g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s$; this
composite is the canonical map of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Its evaluation $\kappa_N$ at
$(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ is the image of an isomorphism under the exact functor
$\Gamma(s,-)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], hence an isomorphism.

proof.text:
*Part 1.* For $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E\}$, $\iota_N=\kappa_N\circ\operatorname{ins}\circ
\operatorname{res}_{g_s}$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] is a composite of three isomorphisms
(steps 1-3), hence an isomorphism. For $\Lambda=E$, $\iota_N$ is by definition obtained from the
$\iota$ of $\mathcal O_E$ by the rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]: on an object
$K\otimes E$ with $K$ integral it is the image of $\iota_K$ under the rationalization functor, an
isomorphism because functors carry isomorphisms to isomorphisms; on a direct summand $N$ of such an
object (the Karoubi envelope) it is the restriction of $\iota_{K\otimes E}$ to the summand, by naturality,
and a retract of an isomorphism is an isomorphism. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, $\iota_N$ is, by the common-stage
construction [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the image of $\iota_{N'}$ for a stage $N'$ of
$N$ over some $E'$, hence an isomorphism by the case $\Lambda=E'$.

source.place: (1.1.7), p. 151 ('transport de structure'); the step is written by an agent

proof.text:
*Direct-image exchange at finite level.* Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of
finite-type $k_0$-schemes, $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $k$, and $A=A_{E,n}$. All schemes involved
are over $k$ of characteristic $p\neq\ell$, so $\ell$ is invertible on them. By
[def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (1), $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}$ is the ambient exchange
$\Ex^A_{\square_f}$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for the Frobenius square
$\square_f=(f,f,g_Y,g_X,(g_X,f))$, Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] by
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] (3): it is the mate
$Lg_Y^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\eta Lg_Y^*Rf_*}Rf_*Lf^*Lg_Y^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{Rf_*\theta Rf_*}
Rf_*Lg_X^*Lf^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{Rf_*Lg_X^*\varepsilon}Rf_*Lg_X^*$ of the natural isomorphism
$\theta=\theta_{\square_f}:Lf^*Lg_Y^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_X^*Lf^*$ under the adjunction
$Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ (unit $\eta$, counit $\varepsilon$) between $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and
$D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Apply
[lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with $\mathcal C=\mathcal C'=D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$\mathcal D=\mathcal D'=D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $L=L'=Lf^*$, $R=R'=Rf_*$, $G=Lg_Y^*$, $G'=Lg_X^*$:
its mate $\alpha:GR\to R'G'$ is exactly the displayed composite. By
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] (1), $g_Y$ and $g_X$ are isomorphisms of schemes, so by
[lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-equivalence] $G=Lg_Y^*$ and $G'=Lg_X^*$ are equivalences of
categories. Hence $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K)$ is an isomorphism for every
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$.

proof.text:
*Compact-support exchange at finite level.* With $f_0$ as in step 5, choose the compactification
$X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y_0$ of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2)
([def-weil-compactifications-refinements], existing by [prop-compactification-refinement]); $p_0$ is
proper, hence a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes. By definition
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}(K)=Rp_*(b_{g_{\overline X}}(K))\circ\operatorname{FrEx}_{p,*}(j_!K)$
(composed, if $Rf_!$ was formed with another compactification, with the comparison isomorphisms of
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]). The first factor $\operatorname{FrEx}_{p,*}(j_!K)$ is an
isomorphism by step 5 applied to $p_0$. The map $b_{g_{\overline X}}(K):Lg_{\overline X}^*j_!K\to
j_!Lg_X^*K$ is an isomorphism by [lem-trf-open-square-exchange], applicable because the square
$(j,j,g_{\overline X},g_X)$ is Cartesian with $j$ an open immersion by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square];
so $Rp_*(b_{g_{\overline X}}(K))$ is an isomorphism, $Rp_*$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image] being a
functor. Hence $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}(K)$ is a composite of isomorphisms, an isomorphism, for every
$K$ in the domain of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

proof.text:
*Other coefficient rings.* For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K)$ and
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}(K)$ are, by [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], the maps induced on
derived limits [def-weil-derived-limit] (through the Roos triangles of the integral operations
[def-pur-integral-derived-operations]) by the morphisms of inverse systems whose $m$-th components are
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m})$, resp.
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m})$, composed with the identification
isomorphisms by which the integral $Lg^*$, $Rf_*$, $Rf_!$ are obtained from their finite levels. Each
component is an isomorphism by steps 5 and 6 (restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_m$, a functor,
preserves isomorphisms), so by [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] the induced map is an isomorphism.
For $\Lambda=E$ the maps are images of the integral ones under the rationalization functor, or retracts
of such images on direct summands [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], hence isomorphisms; for
$\Lambda=\Qlb$ they are the images of the maps at a stage $E'$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients],
hence isomorphisms.

proof.text:
*Part 2.* Take $f_0=a_{Y_0}:Y_0\to\Spec k_0$ (separated of finite type), so $f=a_Y$, $Y$ of steps 5-7
is $s$, $g_Y$ there is $g_s$ and $g_X$ there is $g_Y$; then $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M)=
\operatorname{FrEx}_{a_Y,*}(M)$ and $\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M)=\operatorname{FrEx}_{a_Y,!}(M)$
[def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport, def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], isomorphisms by steps
5-7. Their source and target lie in the full subcategory $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ (as in
[def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]), and an isomorphism of the ambient category between objects
of a full subcategory is an isomorphism of the subcategory.

source.place: (1.1.14), p. 153; the step is written by an agent

proof.text:
*Part 3.* By [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport],
$\tau_M=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M))\circ\iota_{Ra_{Y*}M}$ and
$\tau_{c,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M))\circ\iota_{Ra_{Y!}M}$. The maps
$\iota_{Ra_{Y*}M}$, $\iota_{Ra_{Y!}M}$ are isomorphisms by part 1 (step 4), and
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], a functor, carries the isomorphisms of part 2
(step 8) to isomorphisms; so $\tau_M$ and $\tau_{c,M}$ are isomorphisms. They are natural in $M$ by
[def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] (composites of natural transformations), hence natural
isomorphisms. Taking the $i$-th cohomology, a functor, gives isomorphisms
$\mathrm H^i(\tau_M):H^i(Y,M)\to H^i(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ and $\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M}):H^i_c(Y,M)\to
H^i_c(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] for every $i$.

split_report.summary: Statement kept. Deligne Weil II (1.1.7) p. 151, (1.1.11) p. 152, (1.1.14) p. 153 (pages checked with pdftotext) only assert the actions by transport of structure, so the proof is written by an agent in 9 steps: the three factors of the point transport iota are isomorphisms (restriction along the automorphism g_s of s_proet; the insertion into the inverse-image colimit, whose index category has an initial object and whose presheaf is already a sheaf by lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image (1); the map induced by the structure isomorphism c, (2)-(3)); FrEx_{f,*} at finite level is the mate of the isomorphism theta of the Frobenius square along the equivalences Lg_Y^*, Lg_X^* (new nodes lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences and lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-equivalence); FrEx_{f,!} is FrEx_{p,*} followed by Rp_* of the open-square isomorphism b (lem-trf-open-square-exchange); O_E by derived limits (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso, Pretriangulated.isIso₁_of_isIso₂₃), E and Qlb by functoriality and retracts; tau = Fib_s(FrEx) o iota. stmt_deps unchanged.
